summary: Very diversified: 1791 holdings; the top ten are only 28%.
Trades a lot: about 54% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 5.4 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are similarly priced and more profitable.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 3 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1957; Wharton. Founded Gotham Capital in 1985 with about $7 million, returned all outside money in 1995, and taught value investing at Columbia Business School for over 20 years. Wrote You Can Be a Stock Market Genius (1997) and The Little Book That Beats the Market (2005).
profile.approach: The 'magic formula': rank companies on how cheap they are (earnings yield) and how good they are (return on capital), and own many of the best-ranked. Gotham Asset Management applies this systematically across long and short funds.
known: Gotham Capital returned 50% a year before fees (30% after) from 1985 to 1994.
profile.note: Gotham holds well over a thousand stocks and also sells short, which the 13F does not show; read the holdings as a rules-based basket, not a list of conviction picks.
